questions.title: Hitting a Second Ball Near Water
questions.question: If your ball goes into the pond or a place marked with red sticks, can you hit a second ball just in case (a provisional ball)?

choices.text: Yes, you can always hit a second ball anywhere.
No, you cannot hit a second ball if your ball might be in a pond or by red sticks.
Yes, but only if you cannot find your ball.
Only if you are playing with a team.

questions.explanation: You cannot hit a provisional ball if you think your ball is in a pond or marked by red sticks. For these places, you must follow special rules to play your next shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A second ball you play just in case your first ball is lost or out of bounds.
Parts of the course like ponds, rivers, or places marked with red or yellow sticks.

questions.teachingTip: Take kids to a pond or area marked with red sticks and act out what happens when a ball goes in. Show that you do not play a provisional ball, but follow relief procedures.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they can always play a provisional ball if they cannot see their ball.
Kids might not know that water marked with red or yellow sticks has special rules.

questions.title: Provisional ball and penalty areas
questions.question: If your ball goes into a penalty area, such as a pond marked with red stakes, can you decide to play a provisional ball?

choices.text: Yes, you can always play a provisional ball in any situation.
No, you cannot play a provisional ball if your ball might be in a penalty area.
Yes, but only if your ball is not found.
Only if you are playing in a team competition.

questions.explanation: You are not allowed to play a provisional ball when your ball is likely in a penalty area. Instead, you must use the penalty relief options.
